## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Hive Scale
where: ScaleRepository (uses), src/persistence/repositories.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
private readonly items = new Map<string, ScaleRecord>();
=====SOURCE-END=====
graph:

- <- CALLS Method ScaleService.linkScale
- <- CALLS Method ScaleService.listScales

### B
concept: Hive
where: ScaleService (uses), src/business/scaleService.ts, component business

=====SOURCE-BEGIN
const hive = this.hives.findById(hiveId);
=====SOURCE-END=====

- class ScaleService (node f7e458262ae72ac4): layer domain, component business, fan-out 12, fan-in 0
- -> CALLS Method HiveRepository.findById
- -> CALLS Method InspectionRepository.findByHive
- -> CALLS Method ScaleRepository.findByHive
- -> CALLS Method ScaleRepository.findBySerial
- -> CALLS Method ScaleRepository.save

response.rationale: A is the hive scale, a weighing device. ScaleRepository (node 18ab235f6c31a91a) stores it as `private readonly items = new Map<string, ScaleRecord>();` and ScaleService reaches it through ScaleRepository.findBySerial and ScaleRepository.findByHive, so a scale has its own serial number and its own repository. B is the hive itself. In ScaleService (node f7e458262ae72ac4) it is loaded with `const hive = this.hives.findById(hiveId);`, which goes through a separate HiveRepository. The method name ScaleService.linkScale and the lookup ScaleRepository.findByHive show that a scale is linked to a hive; it is not the hive under another name. Sharing a hive id makes them related, not the same concept.
